notes: cutpurses work the toll queue; a bravo duels anyone who refuses to pay. The guilds' bravo keeps the toll table by day and asks five marks of whoever touches it; whoever walks on past the table without paying has it out with him. The cutpurses work the queue on the landward approach.
smugglers with a dropout Sayer casting Hush; their signal-crib for the Undercroft run is under a stone at the beacon's foot

gutter drakes in the hull. Not while a new mage is learning at the Lamp and leaving by the road 27 m off the hull (docs/FIGHTING_STYLE_STARTS.md 3.3a): first_mage stands its own two drakes on the Lamp's shore.
leech-hounds come up the channel at night

none; a book and a side quest. The book is the hermit's own exercise book from his clerking years, the name on its flyleaf boxed out, read on his crate where he leaves it; the side quest is his (npcs/poi_people.json, quests/side_2.json).
gutter drakes on the holm, up from the cellars; the egg-collectors' warm-egg board lies inside (interiors/places_brightwater.json), and the Warm Egg sends you down through the hinge-less door
cutpurses use the cellars after dark. The Quiet Hands' fair copy of the masons' lintel lies where the copyist left it (the POI's hook).
The garrison is the site's own (pois/brightwater.json site.garrison). What lies at the gate: a writ the Captain tore across.
none; the bleachers at work (npcs/poi_people_brightwater.json). The Company's writ is nailed to the hut.
smugglers at the mouth by night, bringing the boats' goods up the slide; a Hushed sayer keeps the throat quiet
cutpurses after dark, sent by an Undercroft buyer to prise a singing slate out of the face; the Slades' thousand-book is on the splitting-bench by day and night
none; the clerk at his window (npcs/poi_people_brightwater.json), and his letters to the Row, sealed and unsent, on the step
none by day; the pin-drawer is the Charter Pins' own (quests/the_map.json). A receipt for the third pin is pushed into the crack.
none; a Merrowhithe smoker's note pinned to the third arch's pier, and Ottilie Gannet at the arches' foot (npcs/poi_people_brightwater.json)
gutter drakes after dark, nesting in the wet under the last pile (the POI's hook: the pile wet to the knee in a dry field)
resurrection men from the Undercroft at the portal by night, with their dark lanterns; at dusk two of the struck come out to the Needle to read
brass-takers at the shaft head after dark, carrying up the night's pigs of brass; one keeps the lamp on the headframe
the Tallymen's clerk's schedule lies in the nettles by his hat, where he dropped both coming down
gutter drakes nest in the barge's wet hold under the oak after dark
